questions.prompt: What do the columns of the standard matrix of a linear map represent?
questions.answer:
The columns are the images of the standard basis vectors. If \(T:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), then the standard matrix is
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}|&|&&|\\ T(\mathbf e_1)&T(\mathbf e_2)&\cdots&T(\mathbf e_n)\\ |&|&&|\end{pmatrix}.
\]

questions.prompt: What size matrix represents a map \(T:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^2\)?
questions.answer: The number of columns is the input dimension and the number of rows is the output dimension. Therefore the matrix has \(2\) rows and \(3\) columns, so it is \(2\times3\).

questions.prompt: Find the standard matrix for \(T(x,y)=(3x,5y)\).
questions.answer:
Compute the basis images:
\[
T(1,0)=(3,0),\qquad T(0,1)=(0,5).
\]
Place them as columns:
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\0&5\end{pmatrix}.
\]

questions.prompt: For \(A=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\4&0\end{pmatrix}\), what are \(T(\mathbf e_1)\) and \(T(\mathbf e_2)\)?
questions.answer:
The first column is \(T(\mathbf e_1)\) and the second column is \(T(\mathbf e_2)\). Hence
\[
T(\mathbf e_1)=(2,4),\qquad T(\mathbf e_2)=(-1,0).
\]

questions.prompt: Find the matrix of \(T(x,y)=(x+y,2x-y)\).
questions.answer:
Evaluate the standard basis vectors:
\[
T(1,0)=(1,2),\qquad T(0,1)=(1,-1).
\]
These become columns, so
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\2&-1\end{pmatrix}.
\]

questions.prompt: The matrix \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&2\\0&3&-1\end{pmatrix}\) represents \(T:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^2\). Find \(T(x,y,z)\).
questions.answer:
Multiply \(A\) by the coordinate column:
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&0&2\\0&3&-1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}x+2z\\3y-z\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Therefore \(T(x,y,z)=(x+2z,3y-z)\).

questions.prompt: A linear map satisfies \(T(1,0)=(2,-1,0)\) and \(T(0,1)=(4,3,5)\). Write its standard matrix.
questions.answer:
The outputs are the columns of the matrix. Since the output vectors have three components and there are two input basis vectors,
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}2&4\\-1&3\\0&5\end{pmatrix}.
\]

questions.prompt: For \(A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\-1&3\end{pmatrix}\), compute the output for input \((4,-2)\).
questions.answer:
Multiply:
\[
A\begin{pmatrix}4\\-2\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}2(4)+1(-2)\\-1(4)+3(-2)\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}6\\-10\end{pmatrix}.
\]
So the output is \((6,-10)\).

questions.prompt: Find the standard matrix of \(T(x,y,z)=(x-z,2x+y,3z)\).
Given \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\\5&6\end{pmatrix}\), express \(T(x,y)\) as a linear combination of the columns.
questions.answer:
The columns are \((1,3,5)\) and \((2,4,6)\). Therefore
\[
T(x,y)=x(1,3,5)+y(2,4,6).
\]
Componentwise this is \((x+2y,3x+4y,5x+6y)\).

questions.prompt: A map has matrix \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}\). Verify from columns that \(T(3,4)=3T(1,0)+4T(0,1)\).
questions.answer:
The columns give \(T(1,0)=(1,0)\) and \(T(0,1)=(1,2)\). Then
\[
3T(1,0)+4T(0,1)=3(1,0)+4(1,2)=(7,8).
\]
Also
\[
A\begin{pmatrix}3\\4\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}7\\8\end{pmatrix}.
\]
They match.

questions.prompt: Explain why a \(3\times2\) matrix cannot represent a standard-coordinate map from \(\mathbb R^3\) to \(\mathbb R^2\).
questions.answer: A standard matrix has one column for each input coordinate and one row for each output coordinate. A map \(\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^2\) needs \(3\) columns and \(2\) rows, so its matrix is \(2\times3\). A \(3\times2\) matrix instead represents a map \(\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^3\).

questions.prompt: A linear map sends \((1,1)\) to \((3,5)\) and \((1,-1)\) to \((1,-1)\). Find its standard matrix.
questions.answer:
Let \(T(1,0)=\mathbf a\) and \(T(0,1)=\mathbf b\). Then
\[
\mathbf a+\mathbf b=(3,5),\qquad \mathbf a-\mathbf b=(1,-1).
\]
Add equations: \(2\mathbf a=(4,4)\), so \(\mathbf a=(2,2)\). Then \(\mathbf b=(1,3)\). Therefore
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\2&3\end{pmatrix}.
\]

questions.prompt: Find the matrix of the map that projects \((x,y,z)\) onto the \(xz\)-plane by removing the \(y\)-component.
questions.answer:
The map is \(T(x,y,z)=(x,0,z)\). Compute basis images:
\[
T(1,0,0)=(1,0,0),\quad T(0,1,0)=(0,0,0),\quad T(0,0,1)=(0,0,1).
\]
Thus
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&0&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]

questions.prompt: For which \(a\) does \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1&a\\2&4\end{pmatrix}\) send \((1,-1)\) to \((0,-2)\)?
questions.answer:
Compute
\[
A\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1-a\\2-4\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1-a\\-2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Set this equal to \((0,-2)\). The second component already matches, and the first gives \(1-a=0\). Hence \(a=1\).

questions.prompt: Find all \(b\) such that \(A=\begin{pmatrix}b&1\\1&b\end{pmatrix}\) sends both \((1,1)\) and \((1,-1)\) to scalar multiples of themselves.
questions.answer:
Compute
\[
A(1,1)=(b+1,b+1)=(b+1)(1,1),
\]
so \((1,1)\) always stays on its line. Also
\[
A(1,-1)=(b-1,1-b)=(b-1)(1,-1).
\]
This also always stays on its line. Therefore every real value of \(b\) works.

questions.prompt: A matrix has columns \(\mathbf c_1=(1,2)\), \(\mathbf c_2=(0,1)\), and \(\mathbf c_3=(3,-1)\). Find the input \((x,y,z)\) that maps to \(2\mathbf c_1-\mathbf c_2+4\mathbf c_3\).
questions.answer:
Matrix multiplication forms
\[
T(x,y,z)=x\mathbf c_1+y\mathbf c_2+z\mathbf c_3.
\]
To get \(2\mathbf c_1-\mathbf c_2+4\mathbf c_3\), choose the coordinates that are the coefficients: \(x=2\), \(y=-1\), \(z=4\). The input is \((2,-1,4)\).

questions.prompt: A student writes the basis-vector images as rows instead of columns. Diagnose the error for \(T(1,0)=(2,3)\), \(T(0,1)=(5,7)\).
questions.answer:
The correct matrix uses those images as columns:
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}2&5\\3&7\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The row version would be \(B=\begin{pmatrix}2&3\\5&7\end{pmatrix}\). It gives \(B(1,0)=(2,5)\), not \((2,3)\). Therefore the row placement represents a different map.

questions.prompt: Prove that knowing a linear map on a basis determines its matrix and its value on every vector.
questions.answer:
Every vector in \(\mathbb R^n\) can be written uniquely as
\[
\mathbf v=x_1\mathbf e_1+\cdots+x_n\mathbf e_n.
\]
Linearity gives
\[
T(\mathbf v)=x_1T(\mathbf e_1)+\cdots+x_nT(\mathbf e_n).
\]
So the outputs of the basis vectors determine every output. Placing those outputs as columns gives the matrix that performs exactly this linear combination.

questions.prompt: Can two different standard matrices represent the same linear map \(\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^2\)? Justify your answer.
questions.answer: No. If two standard matrices \(A\) and \(B\) represent the same map, they give the same outputs for \(\mathbf e_1\) and \(\mathbf e_2\). But those outputs are exactly the columns of the standard matrix. Therefore column 1 of \(A\) equals column 1 of \(B\), and column 2 of \(A\) equals column 2 of \(B\). Hence \(A=B\).
